title: Sparkline paper-scout: kv-cache stitching & lightweight eval ideas
content:
Quick scout log — skimming + immediate todo (raw, noisy).

Context: sprint goal is to shave tail latency for long-context chat by mixing prefix caching with small on-the-fly local KV windows. Want cheap evals that catch regressions early. Notes pulled from 3 papers + a workshop talk I watched.

Paper sketches and takeaways:
1) Sparse KV stitching (paper A, arXiv link above)
- Idea: keep dense prefix KV snapshot + sparse delta windows for recent tokens. Merge when patch density exceeds threshold.
- Perf: authors report 18–22% token savings for dialogs with repeated sections. Latency hit depends on merge frequency; async merge helps.
- Takeaway: promising when context has repeated templates. Our workloads (support chat) fit pattern ~30% of sessions.
- Questions: what is merge memory overhead for 1M-token sessions at 8-bit quant? How does it interact with our continuous-batching logic?

2) Lightweight eval harness (workshop note + repo GH-PR-9821)
- Goal: able to run 500 mini-prompts across model variants in <5 minutes with reproducible metrics (perplexity not enough).
- Useful signals: structured response checks, token-level timing percentiles (50/95/99), and pass/fail on hallucination probes.
- My sketch: create a 3-tier eval: smoke (fast lat metrics), quality (100 examples, semantic checks), stress (long sessions, KV eviction scenarios).
- Implementation notes: use cached embeddings and deterministic sampling (seeded top-k) for faster repeatability.

3) Batching policy heuristics (talk by Kenji)
- Dynamic batch cutoffs based on tail-latency budget and request urgency header (we already have this header in prod).
- Empirical rule: if 95th latency target < 120ms, cap batch size at 4 for 8k-seq; otherwise allow burst.
- Combine with prefix-cache hit rate to expand batch when reuse high.

Short experiments to try (priority order):
- EXP-1 (2d): Prototype sparse-delta KV layer in local runtime (no kernel changes). Track memory delta and per-step KV merge time. Metric: net per-token latency change at 95p on 4 GPU types.
- EXP-2 (3d): Lightweight eval harness: shell script to run smoke+quality tiers against current prod model and candidate quantized variant. Goal: <7 min run time for smoke+quality with per-route dashboard.
- EXP-3 (4d): Policy sim — replay 10k real sessions and simulate batching rules with/without prefix-cache to estimate throughput drop and tail latency.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Eviction strategy: LRU vs time-decay vs usage-weighted for sparse deltas? Which best preserves key re-use for FAQs?
- Interaction with quantization: 4-bit kernels might make merge cheaper but memory layout changes can break cheap pointer swaps. Need small microbench.
- Safety/regression detection: what thresholds in lightweight eval should block rollouts? Suggest blocking if quality metric drops >2% absolute or 95p latency increases >15%.

Notes-to-self (todo list):
- Talk to Kenji about available kernel telemetry (how to measure merge cost inside runtime). @Kenji S.
- Spin up dedicated 1-GPU dev rig to run EXP-1. Use sample_traffic_oct2025 for session archive.
- Add 20 template-based prompts to the lightweight eval probe set (customer-support oriented).
- Write quick design doc for sparse-delta API (surface: attach/detach snapshot, merge_trigger). Draft by 2026-04-06.

Random heuristics observed:
- If prefix-hit-rate > 0.65 and avg-session-length > 1800 tokens, merging every 12k tokens gives good balance. (purely anecdotal — measure!)
- For smoke eval, 30 prompts covering control-flow + hallucination probes catches ~75% of obvious regressions in our runs.

Links I skimmed:
- Sparse stitching paper (above).
- Microkernels talk recording: slack link SLACK-CU-thread-xyz789 (Kenji).
- Lightweight eval repo: GH-PR-9821 (branch: fast-smoke).

End of pass. Will iteratively refine and surface a concise design doc for sync on Thu standup.

-- Zaid
